sentences.text:
Challenge in this appeal is the award that is passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Bengaluru, In MVC No.5809/2019 dated 07.03.2020.
This is the claimant's appeal.
3. The appellant projecting that he sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred in the year 2019 filed a petition claiming compensation of 20,00,000/- in total.
The tribunal gave a finding that he is entitled to a sum of 3,51,000/- as compensation.
4. Arguing the matter, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the tribunal awarded meager sum as compensation.

The appellant as an agriculturist was earning 20,000/- per month by the date of accident, however, tribunal took the national income of the NC: 2026:KHC:6812 HC-KAR appellant as 10,000/- per month only, which is unjustifiable.

Learned counsel submits that the accident occurred in the year 2019 and for the relevant period Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is taking the notional income as 14,000/- per month for settlement of claims and at least said figure should have been considered by the tribunal.

Learned counsel also states that though PW2 stated that the disability in respect of whole body is 12%, the tribunal took the disability as 10%
in respect of whole body which is not fair.
Learned counsel further contends that the tribunal has not awarded the required sum and therefore allowing the appeal the amount sought for may be granted.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that by the evidence of PW2 itself it is clear that the fracture is united and thus the appellant does not suffer with any disability as he contended.
NC: 2026:KHC:6812 HC-KAR Learned counsel also states that the compensation granted by the tribunal is justifiable.
6. There is no denial of the fact that the appellant sustained fracture of left femur.
Equally there is no denial of the fact that the appellant underwent surgery during the course of treatment.
Considering the evidence of PW2 and other material produced, the tribunal took the disability in respect of whole body as 10%, which requires no interference.
7. So far as occupation and earnings of the appellant are concerned, appellant failed to produce any proof that he holds agricultural land and he is an agriculturalist by profession.
He also failed to establish that he was earning 20,000/- per month.
But considering the submission that is made by learned counsel for the appellant, this Court is of the view that the notional income of the appellant is required to be taken as 14,000/- per month.

Thus, taking the notional NC: 2026:KHC:6812 HC-KAR income as 14,000/- and without disturbing the other parameters i.e. application of appropriate multiplier '5' and disability in respect of whole body as 10%, the compensation which the appellant is entitled to receive towards loss of future earnings comes to 84,000/-
(14,000/-x12x5x10%).
The tribunal granted a sum of 60,000/- only towards loss of future earnings.
Thus, appellant is entitled to an additional sum of 24,000/- (84,000/- minus 60,000/-) towards loss of future earnings.

sentences.text: Exhibiting an opinion that appellant might have lost his earnings for four months, the tribunal granted a sum of 40,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period.
However, taking the notional income as 14,000/-, the compensation which the appellant is entitled to receive towards loss of income during laid up period comes to 56,000/- (14,000 x 4).

Thus, the additional sum which the appellant is entitled NC: 2026:KHC:6812 HC-KAR to receive towards loss of income during laid up period is 16,000/- (56,000/- minus 40,000/-).
9.
The tribunal failed to award any compensation for the expenditure which the appellant would have incurred for transportation during the period of treatment.
This Court is of the view that appellant is entitled to a sum of 10,000/- towards transportation charges.
The compensation granted by the tribunal under all other heads is justifiable.

Therefore, the sum which the appellant is entitled to receive apart from the sum that is awarded as compensation by the tribunal is 50,000/-
(24,000/- + 16,000/- + 10,000/-).
10.
Hence, the appeal is disposed of with the following ORDER i.
Appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The compensation that is granted by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangaluru through orders NC: 2026:KHC:6812 HC-KAR in MVC No.5809/2019 dated 07.03.2020 is enhanced by 50,000/-
iii.
The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iv. Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
v. On such deposit, appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount.

Sd/-
(DR.CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA) JUDGE AP
